extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX Coordinators, and other recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recipients (schools and postsecondary institutions) and employees on obligations under Title IX concerning students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, including notification duties, required information, reasonable modifications, coordination, privacy, and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee obligation to provide Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the employee reasonably believes that the Title IX Coordinator has been notified of the student's pregnancy or related conditions, when a student or a person with a legal right to act on behalf of the student informs an employee of the student's pregnancy or related conditions, the employee must promptly provide the student (or their legal representative) with the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and inform that person that the Title IX Coordinator can coordinate specific actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure the student's equal access to the education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The employee does not need to ask whether the Coordinator has been notified; reasonable belief may come from the student's statement or from the Coordinator informing staff that the student has been approved for modifications. Example: if a student only says, 'I'm letting you know I'm pregnant,' the employee must provide the Coordinator contact; if a student says they are already working with the Title IX Coordinator, no further obligation under §106.40(b)(2). The Department prefers erring on providing information rather than withholding it. Training on this duty can be minimal and incorporated into broader Title IX training (see §106.8(d)(1)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No documentation requirement for employee's provision of information; privacy protections for voluntary records
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must comply with final §106.40(b)(2) but the provision does not require documentation of compliance. Any records maintained voluntarily by a recipient relating to Title IX compliance would be subject to the disclosure restrictions of §106.44(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should be aware that voluntarily maintained records are protected under §106.44(j) (with exceptions). The discussion of §106.44(j) explains disclosure restrictions and privacy safeguards; recipients must inform students/their representatives of those protections when providing information under §106.40(b)(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from punishment or retaliation for seeking or obtaining an abortion
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not punish or retaliate against a student solely for seeking or obtaining an abortion; protections discussed in the application of the definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions' and §106.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure their policies and staff actions do not discipline or refer students to law enforcement on the basis of pregnancy-related conduct (including seeking an abortion), as doing so would violate Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to promptly take specified actions under §106.40(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Title IX Coordinator is notified of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the recipient must promptly take the steps specified in §106.40(b)(3), including implementing reasonable modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptness is a fact-specific inquiry depending on factors such as the student's needs, the substance and timing of the requested modification, and characteristics of the education program or activity. Recipients are not required to provide modifications that they can demonstrate would fundamentally alter the nature of the education program or activity. Recipients should consider the importance of access to ensure modifications do not impede academic progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage early notification but respond regardless of notice timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should encourage students to notify the Title IX Coordinator as early as possible so the recipient has time to review requests and provide reasonable modifications; however, no matter when a student notifies the Coordinator, a recipient must respond promptly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may be unable to give advance notice for many reasons (sudden needs, decision time, lack of awareness). Recipients must therefore be prepared to act even when notice is short or belated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-burden reasonable modifications and continued access
rubrics_metrics.description: Many reasonable modifications can be offered and implemented with relatively little administrative effort (e.g., allowing a student to drink, eat, sit, or stand during class). A student may return to the Coordinator later if further needs emerge, and the recipient must take additional actions consistent with §106.40(b)(3)(ii)-(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should prepare to provide simple accommodations promptly and to reassess and expand accommodations as needed without imposing procedural hurdles that would impede access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to act; Title IX Coordinator to coordinate and retain oversight (delegation allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is responsible for taking the specific actions under §106.40(b)(3) to promptly and effectively prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access once notified. The Title IX Coordinator must coordinate these actions; the Coordinator may delegate duties to designees but retains ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may delegate tasks to appropriate staff or departments to make implementation flexible and efficient (consistent with §106.8(a)(2)). If the Title IX Coordinator has a conflict of interest in a particular complaint, they must be prohibited from serving as investigator or decisionmaker in that instance and an alternate must be substituted per §106.45(b)(2). Title IX Coordinators must receive training on bias (§106.8(d)(2)(iii) and (4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness requirement for recipient actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's actions under §106.40(b)(3) must be fully and effectively implemented and serve their intended purposes to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness includes ensuring staff comply with assigned roles and removing structural or resource barriers to compliance. Examples of ineffective implementation include a teacher refusing a granted restroom accommodation or a broken keypad preventing access to a lactation space; recipients must remedy such failures to ensure effective implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training burden limited: employees need only convey two pieces of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final regulations, employees are asked to share only two pieces of information with students when informed of pregnancy or related conditions: (1) the Title IX Coordinator's contact information; and (2) that the Title IX Coordinator can coordinate specific actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training on this matter, as required by §106.8(d)(1)(iii), will likely require limited time and can be incorporated into existing Title IX or related trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of information the Title IX Coordinator must provide upon notification (§106.40(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the Title IX Coordinator must inform the student and their legal representative (as applicable) of the recipient's obligations under §§106.40(b)(1)-(5) and §106.44(j) and provide the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice should cover the recipient's obligations regarding reasonable modifications, voluntary leave, access to lactation space, the general right not to be discriminated against due to pregnancy/related conditions, limits on certifications to participate, where to find Title IX policy and grievance procedures, and privacy/disclosure protections. The Department declines to limit required information (e.g., excluding lactation info after miscarriage) because providing full information empowers students to make informed choices; providing this information does not obligate students to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of grievance procedures and remedial steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures under §106.45 (and, if applicable, §106.46 for postsecondary sex-based harassment) apply to pregnancy-related issues. If a student notifies the recipient that it has failed to implement a reasonable modification or make a lactation space available, the recipient must take additional steps consistent with §106.44(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on facts, grievance procedures guide investigation and resolution; if a determination of sex discrimination is made, the Title IX Coordinator must coordinate remedies and prompt effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue. Supportive measures under §106.44(g) may be required even absent a complaint, and recipients must respond promptly and effectively under §106.44(a) and (f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to align pregnancy and disability procedures when consistent with Title IX and disability laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use the same or similar processes for pregnancy and disability accommodations as long as doing so is consistent with the Title IX regulations and applicable disability laws (Section 504, ADA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recipients elect to align processes, staff assigned must still comply with §106.40(b)(3)(i) and other Title IX duties, and the Title IX Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight per §106.8(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting information (syllabi/websites) permitted but not sufficient alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not prohibited from posting information about availability of pregnancy-related modifications on syllabi or websites, but the Department does not consider such non-individualized notifications sufficient by themselves to ensure students learn about time-sensitive Title IX rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may supplement individual notifications with website/syllabus postings, but must still ensure individualized communication when a student notifies staff or the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: provision targets students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision focuses on students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions to prevent obstacles to education related to those conditions and associated with sex characteristics; it does not require immediate notification for students who are not pregnant (e.g., partners, adoptive parents) about pregnancy-specific rights that do not apply to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains the rationale for limiting the immediate notice requirement to pregnant students and those experiencing pregnancy-related conditions while recognizing the importance of equal access for others in other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and reasonableness: requirement is within Title IX authority and not unduly burdensome
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department finds the requirement to inform students of recipient obligations under §106.40(b)(3)(i) to be within its regulatory authority under Title IX and not unduly costly or burdensome; the information can often be provided in a single conversation or standardized written communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites precedent and longstanding requirements to provide Title IX information and provides a Regulatory Impact Analysis addressing costs and benefits. Recipients need not await separate rulemaking to implement these pregnancy-related clarifications.
